title: How Lost in Meditation was written; lyricist Lou Singer
summary: All his tunes were played on trombone at home, notated and shown to Duke; Lou Singer was a Mills piano-part man.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I see. And then, 'Lost in Meditation?' How about that -- how did that get written?

Well, the same way. All my tunes, I used to always let Duke hear, you know? Since I was in the band and he was recording pretty near, to be thankful that he would record them, and so I would play them for him and if he liked it, he'd arrange and record it.
Did you always write it down first? Did you always write the music down first before you played it, or did you sometimes play it without writing it down.
No, I played it and then I wrote the -- as soon as I played it in the house, I wrote down the melody, you know?
Juan always played his tunes on his trombone -- we never had a piano.
No, I never had a piano, no. I always used to do them on the trombone.
Played all the tunes on his trombone.
The lyric writer, perhaps, of Lost in Meditation, was Singer. There are four names; Tizol, Ellington, Singer and Mills. In Lost in Meditation. Singer? S-i-n-g-e-r.
I know he was working for Duke and Irving Mills in the publishing company.

He used to make piano parts for the publishing companies and so forth. But Lou Singer -- he was on a couple of tunes of mine, though I have forgotten the names, and I guess that's why it's written in there on that tune.
